name: dggs-biodiversity-bias — why equal-area cells matter for biodiversity (and why DGGS adds shape and hierarchy)
description: A pedagogical and supporting-evidence repository for the EGU 2026 talk EGU26-11348 (Fouilloux et al., LifeWatch ERIC). Six reproducible notebooks: (01) a synthetic mathematical proof that lat-lon grids systematically inflate biodiversity counts toward the equator with up to 23x bias from cell geometry alone; (02) a real-data demonstration on 20,100 Quercus suber GBIF occurrences; (03) cell-shape anisotropy quantification across grid systems; (04) a kernel-footprint comparison showing what an ML model literally sees on lat-lon, Behrmann (cylindrical equal-area), and HEALPix at 65N; (05) a 3-grid synthetic comparison establishing that Behrmann and HEALPix both solve the count bias; (06) a single-panel illustration of HEALPix NESTED hierarchical refinement (parent -> 16 children -> 256 descendants, deterministic bit-shift on the cell index, no reprojection). Together the notebooks make the slide-5 argument that equal-area is a statistical correctness choice and that for AI-ready biodiversity data, cell shape and multi-resolution hierarchy are correctness choices too.
